pairs.locus: Historia Septem Sapientum, Avis (2nd story of 1st sage)
pairs.question: Non vidisti aliquid?
pairs.answer: Domine, quid potui videre? Tota nocte fuerunt tonitrua et coruscationes et pluvie.
pairs.derivation: Husband interrogates the magpie. Dropped the speech-tag framing 'Tunc ille interrogavit picam et dixit.' before the question and 'Tunc pica dixit :' before the answer. The pica's contiguous reply answers by reporting the (faked) stormy night; kept whole through the first full stop.

pairs.locus: Historia Septem Sapientum, Avis (2nd story of 1st sage)
pairs.question: Cur turbasti me dicendo facinora mea marito meo?
pairs.answer: Non, domina, absit! Non ego feci talia, sed pica dixit domino nostro, quem adhuc non habeo notum.
pairs.derivation: Mistress asks her maid why she betrayed her. Dropped tag 'Mulier vero dixit ancille sue:' before the question and 'Ancilla dixit:' before the answer. The maid's reply denies and reattributes the betrayal to the magpie; contiguous through the full stop.

pairs.locus: Historia Septem Sapientum, Catula (2nd story of 2nd sage)
pairs.question: Mi domina, quare ploras?
pairs.answer: Ista catula puella pulcra fuit nimis et filia mea fuit.
pairs.derivation: The young woman asks the old woman why she weeps. Dropped tag 'Cui dixit puella:' before the question and 'Que dixit:' before the answer. Answer trimmed to the first sentence, which states the cause (this dog was my daughter); the rest digresses into the back-story.

pairs.locus: Historia Septem Sapientum, Simia (3rd story of the Queen)
pairs.question: Quid habes, magne imperator, quid fugis?
pairs.derivation: The ape asks the fleeing lion. Dropped tag 'Tunc reperit eum symia et dixit:' before the question and 'Leo dixit:' before the answer. Question kept as the single contiguous utterance; answer is the lion's complete direct reply.

pairs.locus: Historia Septem Sapientum, Striga + Fons (2nd story of the Queen)
pairs.question: Que es tu?
pairs.derivation: The lost prince asks the maiden who she is. Dropped framing 'et clamavit ad eam et ait:' before the question and 'Mox illa:' before the answer. Answer trimmed at the sentence boundary (colon) to the direct reply; the continuation 'sompnus decepit me...' digresses into how she came to be there.

pairs.locus: Historia Septem Sapientum, Striga + Fons (2nd story of the Queen)
pairs.question: Quid times, puer?
pairs.answer: Est mihi amicus fictus et malus et timeo eum.
pairs.derivation: The witch-maiden asks the frightened boy what he fears. Dropped tag 'Et cognovit mulier quod teritus esset et dixit:' before the question and 'Ille respondit:' before the answer. The boy's reply directly states what he fears; contiguous through the full stop.

pairs.locus: Historia Septem Sapientum, Balneator (1st story of 5th sage)
pairs.question: Cur fles?
pairs.answer: Pater tuus fuit dilectus ab omnibus et faciebat legem et iusticiam in populo suo. Nunc autem timeo, ne memoria eius pereat.
pairs.derivation: The prince asks the weeping bath-keeper why he weeps. Dropped tag 'Cui dixit filius regis:' before the question and 'Dixit balneator:' before the answer. Two-sentence reply kept because it is one continuous explanation of the cause of his weeping (praise of the father, then fear his memory will perish).

pairs.locus: Historia Septem Sapientum, Balneator (1st story of 5th sage)
pairs.question: Pro qua causa?
pairs.answer: Quia nequis iungi mulieribus ut mos est.
pairs.derivation: The prince asks for what reason. Dropped tag 'Dixit filius regis:' before the question and 'Ait ille:' before the answer. The bath-keeper's reply gives the reason directly; complete single-sentence answer.
